\chapter{Evaluation}
\label{ch:evaluation}

\section{Setup}
We replayed the edit history of twelve student projects against a test
server. Each replay ran three times per strategy.

\begin{table}[ht]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{lrr}
    \toprule
    Strategy & Median latency (ms) & Memory (MB) \\
    \midrule
    No cache       & 41.0 & 12 \\
    Write-through  &  6.2 & 48 \\
    Write-back     &  5.9 & 51 \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{Latency and memory per strategy.}
  \label{tab:results}
\end{table}

\section{Results}
Table~\ref{tab:results} lists the medians. Both caches cut latency by a
factor of six; write-back saves little over write-through and risks losing
edits on a crash. Figure~\ref{fig:results} plots latency against group size.

\begin{figure}[ht]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.6\textwidth]{figures/results}
  \caption{Latency as the group grows.}
  \label{fig:results}
\end{figure}

Plugging the measured hit rate of $h = 0.93$ into Equation~\eqref{eq:cost}
predicts the observed drop within ten percent.
